items.stem: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals change down the group?
items.answer: it increases
items.markingKey: Outer electrons lost more easily (lower IE).

items.stem: Explain why the reactivity of the Group 2 elements increases down the group.
items.answer: The two outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded, so less energy is needed to remove them (lower sum of first and second IEs).
items.markingKey: further/more shielded [1]; electrons lost more easily [1]

items.stem: Explain why Group 2 elements always form 2+ ions.
items.answer: They have two outer-shell (s) electrons; removing them gives a noble-gas configuration, but the third IE (from an inner shell) is far too high.
items.markingKey: two outer electrons [1]; third IE very high [1]

items.stem: 0.800 g of strontium reacts completely with excess water. Write an equation and calculate the volume of hydrogen produced at room temperature and pressure, in cm³.
items.answer: Sr + 2H₂O → Sr(OH)₂ + H₂; 219 cm³

items.stem: 0.200 g of calcium reacts completely with excess water. Write an equation and calculate the volume of hydrogen produced at room temperature and pressure, in cm³.
items.answer: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂; 120 cm³

items.stem: A data table in Nairobi lists atomic radii and first ionisation energies of the Group 2 elements: Mg 0.160 nm 738; Ca 0.197 nm 590; Sr 0.215 nm 550; Ba 0.217 nm 503 kJ mol⁻¹. (a) Describe and explain the trend in atomic radius. (b) Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium with steam. (c) Predict a property of radium, the element below barium.
items.answer: (a) Increases: extra shell each period. (b) Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂ (c) Even more reactive with water; lower IE; larger radius.
items.markingKey: (a) Increases: extra shell each period. [2] (b) Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂ [1] (c) Even more reactive with water; lower IE; larger radius. [1]

items.stem: Which Group 2 element has the largest atomic radius?
items.answer: barium
items.markingKey: An extra shell each period down.

items.stem: Why does the first ionisation energy decrease down Group 2?
options: outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded
items.answer: outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded
items.markingKey: Distance and shielding outweigh increased nuclear charge.

items.stem: Explain why the melting points of the Group 2 metals generally decrease down the group.
items.answer: Metal ions become larger with the same charge, so the attraction between the ions and the delocalised electrons weakens.
items.markingKey: larger ions, same charge [1]; weaker metallic bonding [1]

items.stem: A student in Riyadh claims that group 2 elements form 1+ ions because the first ionisation energy is lowest. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. They lose both outer electrons to form M²⁺; the energy is recovered from lattice/hydration enthalpies.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: In a test answer, Amara states: "Reactivity decreases down Group 2 because nuclear charge increases." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Reactivity increases: extra shells and shielding outweigh increased nuclear charge, so electrons are lost more easily.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) Nitrogen dioxide is brown.

items.stem: A student in Bogotá compares the solubilities of Group 2 compounds. Explain how aqueous barium chloride is used to test for sulfate ions.
items.answer: Add dilute HCl then BaCl₂(aq); a white precipitate of BaSO₄ forms because barium sulfate is insoluble.
items.markingKey: acidify then add BaCl₂; white BaSO₄ precipitate [2]

items.stem: Lina heats Group 2 carbonates and nitrates in a school laboratory. (a) Explain why magnesium carbonate decomposes at a lower temperature than barium carbonate. (b) Explain why magnesium hydroxide is used as an antacid but not barium hydroxide.
items.answer: (a) Mg²⁺ is smaller with the same charge, so it has a higher charge density and polarises (distorts) the carbonate ion more, weakening a C–O bond. (b) Mg(OH)₂ is only slightly soluble, a weak alkali, so it neutralises excess acid safely; Ba(OH)₂ is soluble, strongly alkaline and Ba²⁺ is toxic.
items.markingKey: (a) Mg²⁺ smaller/higher charge density; polarises carbonate ion more [2] (b) Mg(OH)₂ sparingly soluble/mild; Ba(OH)₂ soluble/toxic [2]

items.stem: Sofia, a student in Accra, heats 0.840 g of magnesium carbonate, MgCO₃, to constant mass: MgCO₃ → MgO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of solid residue and the total volume of gas produced at r.t.p.

Zara, a student in Santiago, heats 1.000 g of strontium nitrate, Sr(NO₃)₂, to constant mass: 2Sr(NO₃)₂ → 2SrO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Calculate the mass of solid residue and the total volume of gas produced at r.t.p.

A research student in Mumbai studies the thermal stability of strontium nitrate and carbonate. (a) Describe a fair way to compare the thermal stabilities of the carbonates. (b) Describe a test for sulfate ions using a Group 2 compound.
items.answer: (a) Same moles/mass of each, same heating (same burner/flame), time for limewater to turn milky. (b) Acidify with dilute HCl, add BaCl₂(aq): white precipitate of BaSO₄.
items.markingKey: (a) Same moles/mass of each, same heating (same burner/flame), time for limewater to turn milky. [2] (b) Acidify with dilute HCl, add BaCl₂(aq): white precipitate of BaSO₄. [2]

items.stem: Which Group 2 element reacts most vigorously with water?
items.answer: barium
items.markingKey: Reactivity increases down the group.

items.stem: Predict which of magnesium and strontium has the greater reactivity with water, and explain your answer in terms of atomic structure.
items.answer: Strontium. Strontium has more occupied shells, so its outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded; they are lost more easily.
items.markingKey: correct element [1]; extra shell/shielding explanation [1]

items.stem: Predict which of strontium and barium has the greater reactivity with water, and explain your answer in terms of atomic structure.
items.answer: Barium. Barium has more occupied shells, so its outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded; they are lost more easily.
items.markingKey: correct element [1]; extra shell/shielding explanation [1]

items.stem: Kenji adds small pieces of magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium to cold water in a university teaching laboratory. Explain why barium reacts faster with water than calcium.
items.answer: Lower ionisation energies; electrons lost more easily.
items.markingKey: Lower ionisation energies; electrons lost more easily. [2]

items.stem: Yusuf adds small pieces of magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium to cold water in a school laboratory. Write an equation for the reaction of calcium with water and describe what is seen.
items.answer: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂; fizzing, calcium sinks, cloudy white suspension forms.
items.markingKey: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂; fizzing, calcium sinks, cloudy white suspension forms. [2]

items.stem: Mohammed adds small pieces of magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium to cold water in a research laboratory. (a) Write an equation for the reaction of calcium with water and describe what is seen. (b) Predict a property of radium, the element below barium.
items.answer: (a) Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂; fizzing, calcium sinks, cloudy white suspension forms. (b) Even more reactive with water; lower IE; larger radius.
items.markingKey: (a) Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂; fizzing, calcium sinks, cloudy white suspension forms. [2] (b) Even more reactive with water; lower IE; larger radius. [1]

items.stem: Ines adds small pieces of magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium to cold water in a research laboratory. (a) Describe and explain the trend in atomic radius. (b) Explain why barium reacts faster with water than calcium. (c) Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium with steam.
items.answer: (a) Increases: extra shell each period. (b) Lower ionisation energies; electrons lost more easily. (c) Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂
items.markingKey: (a) Increases: extra shell each period. [2] (b) Lower ionisation energies; electrons lost more easily. [2] (c) Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂ [1]

items.stem: Which gas is produced when barium carbonate reacts with dilute nitric acid?
items.answer: carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: BaCO₃ + 2HNO₃ → Ba(NO₃)₂ + H₂O + CO₂.

items.stem: Sofia tests Group 2 compounds with water and dilute acids in a university teaching laboratory. Explain why barium sulfate can be swallowed for X-ray imaging even though barium ions are toxic.
items.answer: BaSO₄ is very insoluble, so almost no Ba²⁺ ions are absorbed; it is dense and absorbs X-rays.
items.markingKey: insoluble; absorbs X-rays [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why the pH of the solution formed by adding Group 2 oxides to water increases down the group. (b) Explain why barium sulfate can be swallowed for X-ray imaging even though barium ions are toxic.
items.answer: (a) The hydroxides become more soluble down the group, so the concentration of OH⁻ ions in solution increases. (b) BaSO₄ is very insoluble, so almost no Ba²⁺ ions are absorbed; it is dense and absorbs X-rays.
items.markingKey: (a) hydroxide solubility increases [1]; higher [OH⁻] [1] (b) insoluble [1]; absorbs X-rays [1]

items.stem: 1.000 g of magnesium carbonate, MgCO₃, reacts exactly with 1.00 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid. Calculate the volume of acid needed, in cm³.
items.answer: 23.7 cm³

items.stem: 2.000 g of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, reacts exactly with 0.50 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid. Calculate the volume of acid needed, in cm³.
items.answer: 108 cm³

items.stem: A lime works in Istanbul heats limestone (CaCO₃) to make quicklime, CaO, which is then slaked with water. (a) Describe one agricultural use of calcium hydroxide and explain the chemistry. (b) Describe how limewater is used to test for CO₂.
items.answer: (a) Neutralises acidic soils: Ca(OH)₂ + 2H⁺ → Ca²⁺ + 2H₂O. (b) Bubble gas through; limewater turns milky (CaCO₃ precipitate).
items.markingKey: (a) Neutralises acidic soils: Ca(OH)₂ + 2H⁺ → Ca²⁺ + 2H₂O. [2] (b) Bubble gas through; limewater turns milky (CaCO₃ precipitate). [2]

items.stem: Grace investigates the reactions of magnesium oxide, hydroxide and carbonate in a quality-control laboratory. (a) Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium oxide with water and predict the pH of the solution. (b) Describe one agricultural use of calcium hydroxide and explain the chemistry. (c) Describe how limewater is used to test for CO₂.
items.answer: (a) MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂; pH about 9 (b) Neutralises acidic soils: Ca(OH)₂ + 2H⁺ → Ca²⁺ + 2H₂O. (c) Bubble gas through; limewater turns milky (CaCO₃ precipitate).
